name: peek-dismiss-escape
description: Escape closes a peek. Asserts the PAGE, not a log line - the parent goes back to its undimmed red once the card is gone. Built on peek-scrim, which established that a peek can be opened here at all: eligibility comes from a favorite rather than pinning, and the gate watches 'Atrium: peek widget showing for parent'.

actions.note: let the startup tab commit before navigating
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot

GATE: the red page really committed as the STARTUP tab. Navigating to it through Cmd+L was tried first and does not work here: the command bar opens and gains key, then the run log shows a dismiss op rather than a commit, which matches the known flakiness of committing the command bar through synthetic input. Making the page the startup tab removes the navigation step entirely.

Hover the link before pressing it. The click alone opened a peek on roughly half of the runs, with the page loaded and the link at exactly these coordinates in every captured frame - so the press was landing without the pointer having settled there. cgevent's move posts a plain mouseMoved with no button.

the link, at coordinates READ OFF a captured frame rather than derived from assumed chrome widths. The first attempt clicked 300,120 from arithmetic (280px sidebar + 40px page padding) and landed just below the link: the sidebar is about 220px here, not 280, and the web pane starts at y=40. A plain click, because MaybeOpenPeek fires on the navigation itself rather than on a modifier.

actions.pattern: Atrium: peek widget showing for parent
actions.note: GATE: a peek really opened. It watches PeekWidget::Show's own line (atrium_peek_widget.mm:527), the sole writer of peek-opened state left in the tree - confirmed by VM run 2026-08-10.
let the open animation finish so the scrim is at full strength rather than mid-fade
the parent WITH a peek over it - 166,0,0 if the scrim is working
Escape is an accelerator on the peek widget itself (atrium_peek_widget.mm, AddAccelerator VKEY_ESCAPE), so it does not depend on the parent page having focus.
let the dismiss animation finish - kPeekDismissDuration is 0.17s, this is generous
the parent after the peek is gone - must be back to 255,0,0

assertions.desc: THE MEASUREMENT: the parent's red must come BACK. With the peek open this strip reads 166,0,0; once the card is gone it must read 255,0,0 again. Measuring the page rather than a log line is deliberate - the app announcing a dismiss does not prove the card left the screen, and the scrim is the thing a user actually sees. Region and its variance rationale are peek-scrim's, verified there.
